# Recant Memory

> Meters an Anthropic-SDK app's model calls on its normal traffic, says what they cost and what Recant would save
> with no change to what the model sees, and applies those savings (cache markers only) on `recant apply`. Also
> managed memory for agents and the measurement that checks both. A library, not a service or an agent framework: it
> calls nothing on its own, sends nothing anywhere, and enforces no spend limit.

Import name `recant`. Python 3.11+. Works on any Python code that calls the Anthropic API through the `anthropic` SDK
(`Anthropic` or `AsyncAnthropic`), sync, async, streaming or a tool loop.

## Add it: the recipe (do exactly this)

1. `pip install "recant[anthropic]"` (or add `recant[anthropic]` to the project's dependencies).
2. Find where the app builds its Anthropic client and wrap it, one line, nothing else changed:

   ```python
   import anthropic, recant
   client = recant.wrap(anthropic.Anthropic())          # sync
   client = recant.wrap(anthropic.AsyncAnthropic())     # async: the same, awaited as before
   ```

   If the client is built in more than one place, wrap each. Keep every call as it is:
   `client.messages.create(...)`, `create(stream=True)`, `client.messages.stream(...)` and `count_tokens` all work
   unchanged. Optional, for two or more agents: put `with client.run("researcher", session=conversation_id):` (or
   `async with`) around one agent's calls and `client.run("writer", ...)` around another's; a call outside any run
   is the job "agent".
3. Run the app as it normally runs. No configuration: the store is `./.recant/` in the working directory (or
   `$RECANT_HOME`), made when the client is wrapped, with its own `.gitignore`.
4. `recant cost`: the first three lines say what was spent, what Recant can save with no change to what the model
   sees, and what that rests on. Below about 20 calls it says it is too early and sizes nothing; run more traffic.
5. `recant apply --dry-run` shows each change; `recant apply` turns the safe savings on. `recant cost` later shows
   the realized saving against the prediction.
6. If anything looks wrong: `recant doctor` (one line per check, and what to do about each problem).

The one rule: **never change prompts, models, `max_tokens`, effort or tools to save cost.** Recant changes only cache
markers by itself; everything else it reports with its dollar size is the app owner's call, after `recant bench`
shows quality holds. To verify the wrapper is a pass-through, `recant off` makes it one (nothing is metered), and
`recant on` turns it back.

For an agent: every command takes `--json` and prints one JSON object naming its schema (`"schema": "recant-cost/1"`,
`recant-apply/1`, `recant-doctor/1`, ...; within a schema version fields are added, never renamed or removed);
`recant cost --json` carries the three lead lines as `summary`. Errors are one line on stderr: exit 1 or 2 is a
problem with the input or the setup (the line says what to change), exit 3 a fault in Recant itself (`RECANT_DEBUG=1`
shows the traceback).

## The cost saver

- `recant.wrap(anthropic_client, store=None, tenant=None, job="agent")` — store default `$RECANT_HOME` or
  `./.recant`, tenant default "default"; `Anthropic` or `AsyncAnthropic`; the same
  `messages.create`, `create(stream=True)`, `messages.stream(...)` and `messages.count_tokens`; meters every call
  (a stream from its final message's usage; thinking tokens as reasoning), carries out the applied safe levers on each
  request, checks the request differs only in cache markers (else sends the host's own). `with client.run("agent",
  session=...)` (or `async with`) is one host run, with its own log, so concurrent runs are metered apart; its first
  argument is the job its calls are reported and sized under (`run("researcher")`, `run("writer")` for two agents),
  wrap's `job` when omitted. A request may hold the SDK's own response blocks (`r.content` in a tool loop); one holding anything but plain
  data and those models (an iterator, a tuple, a file) goes as the host's own objects, untouched, with no lever. Recant's own
  failure on a call or a run (preparing, reading the response or stream, the run's log, the switch) does not raise
  into the host: the call is sent as built and counted in the friction log. `recant.wrap` raises on a store it cannot
  create.
  Recant never times out or retries a call: set your own idle timeout (the SDK's 600 s read timeout does not cut a
  stream that goes silent mid-body, and a mid-body break is not retried); a broken stream is recorded with its error.
- `recant.metering.Meter(layout, tenant)` — for a host on its own client: `run(job)`, `record(job=, model=, usage=,
  session=, system=, messages=, tools=, max_tokens=)` per model call, `tool(...)` per tool call, `close()`.
- `recant.levers.apply(request_dict, recant.costshape.overlay(layout, tenant))` — the safe levers on an
  Anthropic-shaped request; `recant.levers.declare_host(layout, tenant)` once, so the advisor applies them.
- `recant apply [--dry-run] [--json]` — turn on the safe levers that are ready (a job needs 20 runs); `--dry-run`
  shows what each would change in a request.
- `recant doctor [--json]` — version, SDK, store, switch, metering, prices and coverage, checked; exits 1 if any
  needs fixing.
- Every command takes `--store DIR --tenant T` (defaults as for `recant.wrap`).
- `recant cost [--since 7d] [--nightly] [--all] [--revert ID] [--prices FILE] [--json]` — the
  report; with `--nightly`, apply what is eligible and check what was applied (realized against predicted, after 50
  runs or 7 days).
- `--prices FILE` (cost, bench, coverage): JSON keyed by model ID, each row in USD per million tokens: `input`,
  `output`, optional `cache_read`, `cache_write` (both default to `input`), `cache_write_long`, `batch_factor`, and
  `above` + `over` for a second card on prompts over `above` tokens. The library's list (dated 2026-11-05) prices
  the Claude models in `recant.costshape.LIST_PRICES`; an unpriced model is tokens only. `recant cost --json` prints each row in this format.
- `recant.costshape` — `report`, `advise`, `apply`, `check`, `nightly`, `overlay`, `LIST_PRICES` (dated; overridable).
- `recant.billing.reconcile` — the log against the provider's usage report, given a `BillingSource`.
- `recant.metering.from_claude_code(result, meter, billing=)` / `from_agent_sdk(result_message, meter, billing=,
  messages=)` — Claude Code's or the Agent SDK's own end-of-run totals, metered in their own rows (billed, and priced
  at list); no lever applies to them.

## Coverage: what Recant can't see

- `recant.coverage.watch()` — on inside `recant.wrap` (`watch=False` to leave it off; `recant off` stops it): counts
  requests from the host's process to known model-API hosts (`recant/known_hosts.py`) that did not go through Recant,
  and `other` (domain hashed) for an unknown host with a model-call body. Counts only, never content. Hooks httpx and
  httpx2; does not see other HTTP libraries or subprocesses.
- Every report carries a Coverage line; a bench verdict is qualified below 90% of calls or of list-priced cost, and
  gives no overall saving below 50%.
- `recant coverage --usage runs.jsonl [--store DIR --tenant T] [--prices FILE] [--json]` — your own per-run totals
  (`ts`, `model`, `tokens_in` = uncached input as the Anthropic SDK counts it, `tokens_out`, `cache_read`,
  `cache_write`, optional `billed`; a line per call, task or day) against what Recant metered on the same days, by
  model and provider.

## Measuring it yourself

- `recant bench --tasks T --run mod:run_task [--grade mod:grade] [--n] [--calibrate 10] [--mode safe] [--arm-a] [--arm-b]
  [--out DIR] [--yes] [--estimate]` — calibration, frozen hashed predictions, paired arms with alternating order, a
  cache salt and a fresh store per arm; `report.md`/`report.json` with cost, tokens, quality, latency, predicted against
  realized, failures. `--arm-a safe --arm-b safe` is an A/A run; `safe+<lever id>` opts a your-call lever into an arm.
  `client` is a wrapped `AsyncAnthropic` for an `async def run_task`, else `Anthropic`; one client per bench (a sync
  agent in an async host awaits its calls on it). Prints a line per task run. `--report --prices FILE` rebuilds the
  report at another table; frozen are the levers' shares, the dollars on both sides are at the report's prices.
- `recant eval memory --sessions S --make-questions` then `--questions Q [--arms none,history,notes,memory_v2]` —
  memory on your own sessions; questions frozen by hash; mechanical scoring from the `ANSWER:` line (every word of the
  key, single letters and digits as whole words, or the same date or amount; keep keys minimal). `--model` (default `claude-sonnet-5-5`) drafts, writes and
  answers in every arm.
- `recant feedback` — the six-question form and a numbers-only bundle (the store's coverage
  by provider and public model included); every string Recant writes passes an allow-list, the form's answers go in as
  typed, shown first; nothing is sent. The friction log is `~/.recant/friction.jsonl` (or `$RECANT_HOME`).
- `recant off [--meter] | on | status` (or `RECANT=off|meter|on`, which overrides the store's file) — the
  switch, read on every call.
- `recant --version` — version and the commit it was built from (a PyPI release names it, 0.3.3 on); every report
  and bundle header carries them.

## Managed notes (the default memory)

- `recant.notes.TOOL_SPECS` — the `note_fact` and `read_notes` tool definitions (Anthropic tool JSON).
- `recant.notes.handle(tool_name, tool_input, *, layout, tenant, lines, episode_path, today, principal_id)` — runs a
  call: each entry checked against the session's lines, what passes written, refusals named with their reason.
- `recant.notes.session_start(layout, tenant, store, *, principal_id, serve, today, block, model=, client=)` — the
  rendered block for the prefix, after the switch check; None once the scope has moved to extracted memory.
- `recant.notes.INSTRUCTION` — the system-prompt text that tells the agent how to keep notes.
- `recant.episodes.open_session(layout, tenant, day)` — the session file the host appends each turn to;
  `recant.episodes.read_session(layout, tenant, episode_path)` reads it back.

## Extracted memory (the fallback)

- `recant.Store(layout, allowlist)`, `recant.Ledger(layout, allowlist)`, `recant.StoreLayout(root)` (call
  `layout.ensure(tenant)` first) — entries with statuses proposed / probation / live / contested / superseded /
  retired; tasks.
- `recant.extract(layout, tenant, day, machinery=, client=, store=, ledger=, principal_id=)` — a day's sessions into
  proposed entries and tasks, through the caller's `ModelClient`.
- `recant.store.review` — `memory_queue`, `decide_memory`, `task_queue`, `decide_task`.
- `recant.budget.fit(entries, *, family, serve, view, question=None)` — a cached core and a per-question slice as
  deterministic text blocks.
- `recant.machinery.Machinery.seed_defaults(layout)` / `load(layout)` — the default artifact and kernel files.
- `recant.ModelClient` — the protocol: `complete(request) -> Completion`; optional `count_tokens`, `submit`/`poll`.
  `recant.clients.anthropic.AnthropicClient` is the reference implementation.
- `recant.harness` — the eval harness: draft questions from your episodes, judge answers, compare arms against grep.

## Files

- CHANGELOG.md — each version's changes, and the measurements behind the README's numbers and the defaults.
- AGENTS.md — the recipe for a coding agent, and how to run the tests.
- skills/recant/SKILL.md — a Claude Code skill: add Recant to an app and report what it would save.
- README.md — what it is, install, three quickstarts, what leaves the host, what Recant can't see, known limits, the
  client protocol, the formats.
- examples/cost_quickstart.py — a raw-SDK agent with no caching, wrapped; the `recant cost` sequence in its docstring.
- examples/cost_quickstart_async.py — the same agent on the async client, streamed, five tasks in flight.
- examples/notes_agent.py — a complete raw-SDK agent with notes mode on (`--offline` without a key).
- examples/memory_v2_agent.py — the extracted-memory loop: write, extract, review, fit.
- src/recant/defaults/*.yaml — the default machinery files to copy and change.
- src/recant/schemas/*.json — the public formats.

## Rules a caller should know

- Nothing leaves the host; the log keeps counts, tokens, timings and hashes, never the text.
- Recant applies by itself only levers that change cache markers and nothing the model sees; everything else is
  reported with its dollar size and left to the host.
- Notes and memory files are canonical; indexes are derived and disposable.
- A note's value must be in the principal's own words from the session, or in the output of a tool call made in it.
- An entry's status moves only through a logged decision; nothing derived invalidates something stated. No confidence
  score, importance score or TTL exists on an entry, by design.
- The library never refuses a call on cost; put a ceiling, if you want one, around your client.
- Known limits: extracted memory keeps no fact found only in tool output (use notes for those); the reasoning lever
  is offered only where a model can carry it out; notes mode is not in `recant bench` yet; the wrapper is
  Anthropic's only, and a second provider's waits for coverage evidence that a host relies on one.
